title: Free weekend buses in Aldermoor
bodyMd: In 2023 the city of Aldermoor stopped charging fares on its buses on Saturdays and Sundays, while keeping weekday fares unchanged. In the following twelve months, weekend ridership rose by 30 percent. Transport economist Sunniva Dahl argues that the increase came mainly from people who had previously made their weekend trips by car, rather than from people who had walked, cycled or stayed at home, and she concludes that the policy reduced weekend car traffic in the city. Critics of the policy have questioned whether free fares mostly attract drivers or mostly attract people who would have made the trip without a car anyway.
accessibilityText: A short social-science passage. In 2023 the city of Aldermoor made its buses free on Saturdays and Sundays and kept weekday fares unchanged. Weekend ridership rose by 30 percent over the next twelve months. Transport economist Sunniva Dahl argues that the increase came mainly from people who had previously made their weekend trips by car, rather than from people who had walked, cycled or stayed at home, and concludes that the policy reduced weekend car traffic. Critics question whether free fares mostly attract drivers or mostly attract people who would have made the trip without a car anyway.

provenance.notes: Original passage written for this item bank. The city of Aldermoor, the economist and the 30 percent figure are invented; fare-free transit is discussed only in general terms and no published study was consulted or adapted.
